where: Section 1, paragraph on the machining centre
problem: The sentence 'the table carries the work in X and Y' is correct for a vertical machining centre but wrong for a horizontal one. On a horizontal machining centre the table normally gives X (and often Z), while Y is the vertical movement of the spindle head on the column.
fix: Write: 'On a vertical machine the table carries the work in X and Y while Z feeds the spindle down. On a horizontal machine the table gives X and the column or spindle head gives Y and Z, with the spindle pointing sideways at the work.'

problem: 'must not deflect more than a few micrometres' is tighter than a general-purpose machine tool. A machining centre with a stiffness of about 100–200 N/µm deflects roughly 5–10 µm under a 1 kN cut; a few micrometres is a precision-machine figure.
fix: Write: 'The bed and column must deflect less than the tolerance being held — around 10 µm on a general-purpose machine, a few micrometres on a precision one — when the cutting force pushes back.'
